version.changelog: v2.3 quality enhancement - security audit + marketing packaging + slug-content validation

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a local correction-memory helper, but it asks for command execution and mentions callbacks despite describing itself as pure Markdown with no network use.

dimensions.detail: The skill stores memory under ~/evolution-engine and discloses lack of namespace isolation, so cross-project preference pollution is an expected limitation rather than hidden behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest requests read, write, and exec tools, but the documentation says it is pure Markdown and does not need command-line execution. Read/write is expected for local memory; exec is not justified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The input table includes a callback_url for asynchronous completion notification, while the dependency section says the skill makes no network requests. The artifact does not provide network-callback controls or explain what would be sent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent memory is central to the skill and is disclosed, but the artifact gives limited privacy, deletion, retention, and sensitivity guidance for stored corrections, preferences, and reflections.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: record explicit user corrections and reflections into local memory files so the agent can avoid repeated mistakes. Local read/write of ~/evolution-engine files fits that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the extra exec permission before installing; it is not justified by the skill text. If you use it, inspect and periodically clean ~/evolution-engine/memory.md and corrections.md, avoid putting secrets in corrections, and be cautious with any callback_url behavior unless the platform clearly confirms no network request will be made.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: The exec tool request is not supported by the artifact's own pure-Markdown, no-command description, so this concern is accepted as a real authority mismatch.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The callback_url field is inconsistent with the no-network claim; no actual callback implementation is present, so this is an under-disclosure concern rather than evidence of exfiltration.
[SQP-2] expected: Writing corrections.md and memory.md is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but users should treat those files as persistent local records and avoid storing secrets or sensitive personal data.
